A grid or single-column list of cards, with paging, selection that is kept
across pages, and the loading, empty and error states. NAME PROVISIONAL. Section owns these states on a real page; this element
gives them a default look and fires events so a Section can take over.

```html
<prism-card-list label="Resources" selection="multi" total="120" page="2">
  <prism-card type="selectable" kind="collection" value="h-13">…</prism-card>
</prism-card-list>
```

- **Layout.** Columns follow the list's own width (a container query), not
  the screen: under 640px one column, 640 to 1023 two, 1024 to 1279 three,
  1280 and up four. Cards stay at least 280px wide, the gap is space-4 (16px)
  and cards in a row share a height. `columns="1"` pins one column (Aside,
  Drawer, Modal). No masonry.
- **Semantics.** An inner wrapper around the cards is the labelled `list` and
  each card a `listitem` (the card sets its own role). The host has no role,
  so the selected count, pager and status region sit outside the list. Titles stay real headings: give every card
  the same `level`, one below the Section heading. With `total` set, each
  card gets `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize` from the data, not from what
  is on the page.
- **Paging.** Server-side: you swap the children when `prism-card-list-page`
  fires. `page-size` is 12, 24 or 48 (default 24). The pager shows even when
  there is one page. A `pagination` slot replaces it with a real Pagination
  component; `load-more` shows a "Load more" button instead.
- **Selection** uses the same cards, `value` ids and controller as
  `prism-card-group`, multi only (use a group for a single choice). Ids not
  on screen stay selected when the page changes; a visible "N selected" and
  "Clear selection" sit above the cards unless `hide-selection-bar` is set
  or you fill the `toolbar` slot.
- **States** (`state`): `loading` (skeleton cards, list busy, polite
  "Loading"), `refreshing` (cards stay, quiet busy line), `empty` (fill the
  `empty` slot), `no-matches` ("No matches" and Clear filters), `error`
  (what failed and Retry). A single failed card uses `state="error"` on the
  card itself.

declarations.name: tonePalette
declarations.description:
Tone palette for Tag, Badge and Progress. Component-private `--_tone-*`
properties that read the colour roles in tokens (neutral, accent, info,
success, warning, danger), so every tone follows the active theme, light or
dark. The hex after each role is its light sRGB value, used when the token
stylesheet is not loaded. test/tokens.test.mjs reads this file and checks
the fallbacks and every pair, in both themes, on sRGB and Display P3:
low text >= 4.5:1 on its tint and on the page, high text >= 4.5:1 on its
fill, fills >= 3:1 on the page and on the progress track.

  low  = tint fill with coloured text (the default emphasis)
  high = solid fill with its on-colour text

`attr` is the host attribute that carries the tone. The theme reads the four
properties (`--_tone-low-bg`, `--_tone-low-fg`, `--_tone-high-bg`,
`--_tone-high-fg`) from the host.

declarations.description:
A bar that shows how far something has got. Common props: `value`, `max`,
`label`, `tone`. NAMES PROVISIONAL.

- Role `progressbar` with `aria-valuemin` 0, `aria-valuemax` and
  `aria-valuenow`, named by `label`.
- Leave `value` off for an indeterminate bar (`aria-valuenow` is omitted and
  the stripe moves; it stops under reduced motion).
- The label is visible by default. `hide-label` hides it from sight only.
  `show-value` writes the number beside it ("60%", or `value-text` such as
  "3 of 5 steps", which is also the `aria-valuetext`). Colour is never the
  only signal: the fill length and the written value both say it.
- Look: no track border; a faint inset edge shadow on the track. The fill is
  a gradient over its filled width, lighter at the left and the full tone at
  the leading edge (tokens `--prism-progress-fill-lift`,
  `--prism-elevation-track`). Both ends stay 3:1 on the track.
- Use it for a task with a known end. For "loading, no idea how long" use
  a skeleton or an indeterminate bar.
declarations.name: PrismProgress

declarations.description:
Shows that something is running right now: a solid dot that breathes, with
one ring that spreads out of it and fades, like light leaving a prism. Use it
beside a task or card title while a job is in progress, and remove it (or
swap it for a Tag that says "Done") when the job ends.

- `role="status"` with a written label ("Running" by default). The label is
  always in the page for screen readers; `show-label` also shows it.
  Change `label` to say what is running: "Export running".
- Sizes: `sm` 16px, `md` 24px (default), `lg` 40px. The drawing is a 24 unit
  box that scales with the size.
- `tone` colours both the dot and the ring: accent (default), neutral, info,
  success, warning or danger. Use success for "online".
- Motion: the ring grows from the dot's edge (radius 4 to 9) and fades from
  60% to nothing while the dot swells from 4 to 4.6 and back, both in step.
  One pulse takes 1.92s, then it rests for 800ms before the next (a 2.72s
  cycle). In the rest the ring is gone and the dot is still. Under
  `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` it holds still as the dot with a faint
  ring. The dot is always there, so motion is never the only signal.
- It does not show progress. For a known amount of work use Progress.
declarations.name: PrismRunningIndicator

declarations.description:
A switch: an on/off control that takes effect right away, like a light
switch. Use it for a setting ("Auto-refresh"), not for a choice that is only
saved when a form is submitted (use a checkbox there).

- A native `<button role="switch" aria-checked>` in shadow DOM, so Space and
  Enter toggle it and it takes part in the tab order.
- Named by `label` (and any default-slot content). The label is visible by
  default; `hide-label` hides it from sight only.
- Joins the surrounding form: submits `value` (default "on") under `name`
  while on, and nothing while off. Resets to its starting state with the form.
- Fires `input` and `change` after each user toggle.
- Motion: the thumb slides and stretches like a drop of liquid, then springs
  back into shape (about 240ms), while the track fills with the accent from
  the thumb outward. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` it just changes.
- State is never colour alone: the thumb sits at the start when off and at
  the end when on.
- The hover, selected and pressed fills come from the shared state layer.
declarations.name: PrismSwitch

declarations.description:
A short label on an item: a category, a keyword or a property, so people can
find and tell things apart. Names and values follow the Tag page: `job`,
`emphasis` and `tone`. `size` is NAME PROVISIONAL.

Four behaviors, split by what a person can do (not by colour):
- read-only (default): a label, no click.
- `dismissible`: a remove button ("Remove {text}"); fires `prism-tag-remove`.
  The tag does not remove itself: the app decides.
- `selectable`: a toggle button (`aria-pressed`); fires `prism-tag-select`.
- `trigger`: a button that opens something (a Select) and shows a caret in
  the trailing slot; fires `prism-tag-trigger`. It looks like any other Tag.

A Tag never navigates. For a link use a link. For a count or Live / Running
/ Stopped use Badge.

Accessibility: the text is the name and the meaning, so colour is never the
only signal. Put a short word in the tag (a few words, no wrapping). An
icon only helps reading. Interactive tags are at least 24px high even at
`size="sm"` (WCAG 2.5.8).
